# About Me

I'm Daniel, a Colombian development economist with 4+ years of experience in research and applied analysis, particularly at the intersection of data and public policy. My work centers on human development and social protection, especially health, early childhood, youth, and violence prevention. I have developed much of this experience at the IMAGINA Research Center (Universidad de los Andes), the Bogotá District Government, and in collaboration with civil society organizations. I work with Stata, R, Python, and SQL, and I have used large language models to classify and summarize large volumes of policy documents.

Most of my work is used directly by government teams and civil society organizations, so I place special emphasis on ensuring that my analyses are transparent, reproducible, and easy to understand. I'm currently completing an M.A. in Economics at Universidad de los Andes.
